A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRH/PAH study. Their text, equations, figures, Table 1, and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and localized additions and removals.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original experiments on synthetic regression, ResNet-18 image classification and self-supervised learning, and an OpenWebText transformer.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C retain these original experiments, including measured alignment trajectories, representation spectra, and hyperparameter analyses.

M1.justification: The CRH/PAH framework and experimental training procedures are retained. Appendix D's linear-regression factorization is an analytical illustration, not an introduced or modified training algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same fc1, fc2, res1, res2, and llm settings: synthetic regression, CIFAR-10/100 image tasks, and OpenWebText language modeling. Appendix D adds no empirical linear-regression evaluation.

E2.justification: The transformer comparisons retain the random-projection, cross-head, and initial-versus-current representation baselines in Section 6 and Figures 5, 9, and 15. Newly cited research is not introduced as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C.1 retain the alignment metric, normalization and centering, sampling procedures, model configurations, optimizers, and training budgets. Figure 22 discloses weight-decay values for an existing analysis without establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 4 revises the plotted evidence relating rank deficiency to alignment across layers and weight-decay settings. The other sensitivity and supplementary analyses are retained. Figure 22 repeats the revised analysis with a legend rather than adding a separate experiment.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged: transformer plots show variation across eight heads, and Figure 8 summarizes variation across five hidden layers. No new seed counts, repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Figure 4's scatter-point coordinates change, although the reported rank–alignment relationship remains qualitatively similar. Figure 22 reproduces those revised results. The other experimental plots and reported 94% ResNet-18 test accuracy are retained; no general performance improvement is established.

T1.justification: V2 removes Corollary 1 and its proof, corrects the Taylor remainders in Proposition 1's proof, and replaces the erroneous G_b = 0 with G_b = I in the neural-collapse proof. Appendix D.1 adds a linear-regression derivation linked to PAH phase 7. The central theorem statements and phase table remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain six-way CRH alignment, its noise–regularization explanation, PAH phases when alignment breaks, and connections to neural collapse and NFA. The new biological connection extends the implications without redefining these main claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds interpretations involving representation normalization and gradient vanishing or explosion. Appendix A introduces regularization and simplicity bias as possible explanations for invariant versus invertible representations, and the conclusion adds a biological orthogonalization connection. The principal applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Figure 22 newly identifies six weight-decay values and explains that each color represents five hidden layers, extending Figure 4's approximate range description. Figure 8 also drops the erroneous eight-head description of the fully connected network. Appendix C.1 otherwise retains its implementation details.

R1.justification: V2 adds research on representation identifiability, invertibility, regularization, biological orthogonalization, and gradient instability. Appendix A removes the Liu et al. (2022) grokking discussion and Galanti et al. (2021) transfer-learning connection. The central positioning relative to neural collapse and NFA is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. V2 makes localized wording corrections, clarifies parts of Section 5 and Appendix B, revises Appendix A, and adds Appendices C.10 and D. Author affiliation and publication-header text also change.

P2.justification: The paper is reformatted throughout into the ICLR layout, changing typography, text and figure widths, running headers, table styling, and figure placement. Figure 4 changes its markers and horizontal extent, while Figure 22 adds a version with a weight-decay legend.

improvement.justification: V2 improves local mathematical consistency through the Appendix B proof corrections and makes the rank–alignment plot easier to interpret through Figure 22. However, new Appendix D.1, Eq. (135), identifies the full regression solution's Gram matrix with inverse input covariance, which does not generally follow from Eq. (133); that identity describes the whitening factor instead. These useful corrections coexist with a new flaw in the theoretical illustration, leaving the net effect on overall quality unclear.
